Extraterrestrial radiation of an hourly or shorter period

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_ra_period.Rd

Computes the extraterrestrial radiation \(R_a\) received on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere during a period of one hour or less, from the latitude, the longitude, the day of year and the UTC time of the midpoint of the period (FAO-56).

Usage

ef_ra_period(lat, lon, doy, utc_mid, period_hours, standard)

Arguments

lat

Numeric. Latitude \(\phi\) [rad], in [-pi/2, pi/2], positive north. Degrees must be converted (deg * pi / 180, FAO-56 Eq. 22).

lon

Numeric. Longitude \(\lambda\) [rad], positive east, in [-pi, pi].

doy

Numeric. Day of year of the UTC date of the midpoint of the period, whole number in 1-366.

utc_mid

Numeric. UTC time of the midpoint of the period [h], decimal hours in [0, 24). For a period 14:00-15:00 UTC, 14.5.

period_hours

Numeric. Length of the period \(t_1\) [h], in (0, 1] (1 for hourly, 0.5 for 30 min).

standard

Character, no default. Treatment of the periods that contain sunrise or sunset: "fao56" (midpoint criterion of FAO-56: \(R_a = 0\) when the sun is below the horizon at the midpoint, otherwise the full integral) or "asce" (limits of integration set to the sunrise and sunset hour angles, ASCE-EWRI 2005 Eq. 56). See Details.

Value

A numeric vector of extraterrestrial radiation of the period \(R_a\) [MJ m-2 per period] with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim.

Details

$$R_a = \frac{12 \cdot 60}{\pi} G_{sc} d_r \left[(\omega_2 - \omega_1) \sin\phi \sin\delta + \cos\phi \cos\delta (\sin\omega_2 - \sin\omega_1)\right]$$ with \(\omega_1 = \omega - \pi t_1 / 24\) and \(\omega_2 = \omega + \pi t_1 / 24\) (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 28-30). The hour angle at the midpoint \(\omega\) is FAO-56 Eq. 31 (with the seasonal correction \(S_c\) of Eqs. 32-33) written for UTC times and east-positive longitudes, $$\omega = \frac{\pi}{12}\left[\left(t_{UTC} + \frac{12}{\pi}\lambda + S_c\right) \bmod 24 - 12\right]$$ which equals FAO-56 Eq. 31 with \(L_z = 0\) and \(L_m = -\lambda\) (FAO-56 counts longitudes positive west), with the exact 1/15 h per degree instead of 0.06667 (decision WF-10). It is computed by the internal hour angle of ef_solar_geometry().

The same equations are ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eqs. 48 and 50-58 (pp. 39-42), with \(G_{sc}\) = 4.92 MJ m-2 h-1 (= 0.0820 MJ m-2 min-1) and the same coefficients of \(d_r\), \(\delta\), \(S_c\) and \(b\).

Sunrise and sunset (standard, decision WF-10). With standard = "fao56", when the hour angle of the midpoint lies outside \([-\omega_s, \omega_s]\) (Eq. 25), \(R_a = 0\) by definition (FAO-56 midpoint criterion); a period that contains sunrise or sunset gets either its full integral or zero. With standard = "asce", the limits of integration are set with the conditionals of ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eq. 56 (p. 41): \(\omega_1\) and \(\omega_2\) are limited to \([-\omega_s, \omega_s]\) and \(\omega_1 \le \omega_2\), applied to every period as the report allows ("can be applied for all timesteps"); a period entirely below the horizon gets 0 and a period containing sunrise or sunset gets the integral over its sunlit part. The report also states (p. 41) that a midpoint outside \([-\omega_s, \omega_s]\) means \(R_a = 0\); for a period whose midpoint is below the horizon but which contains sunrise or sunset the two statements differ, and Eq. 56 is followed. In polar day (\(\omega_s = \pi\)) there is no sunrise or sunset and the limits are not changed (the literal limitation to \([-\pi, \pi]\) would cut the periods around solar midnight).

Missing values propagate. Values outside the domains above raise earthflux_domain_error; a non-integer doy raises earthflux_input_error.

Verification status

standard = "fao56": VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 28-33; case V15: 14:00-15:00 local standard time on 1 October at 16 degrees 13' N, 16 degrees 15' W gives 3.543 MJ m-2 h-1). standard = "asce": VERIFICADA (ASCE-EWRI, 2005, Eqs. 48, 53-58, pp. 39-42; Eq. 56 for the limits of integration).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_rso(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

deg <- pi / 180
# FAO-56 example 19: 1 October, 14:00-15:00 local standard time in a
# time zone 15 degrees west of Greenwich, i.e. 15:00-16:00 UTC
ef_ra_period(lat = (16 + 13 / 60) * deg, lon = -(16 + 15 / 60) * deg,
             doy = 274, utc_mid = 15.5, period_hours = 1,
             standard = "fao56")
#> [1] 3.543414

# Hourly course of one day (midpoints 00:30 ... 23:30 UTC): the two
# standards differ only in the periods containing sunrise and sunset
fao <- ef_ra_period(lat = -35 * deg, lon = 0, doy = 15,
                    utc_mid = 0:23 + 0.5, period_hours = 1,
                    standard = "fao56")
asce <- ef_ra_period(lat = -35 * deg, lon = 0, doy = 15,
                     utc_mid = 0:23 + 0.5, period_hours = 1,
                     standard = "asce")
which(fao != asce)
#> [1]  6 20
